newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo warring parties agree to three-day truce.
newsitem.headline: Congo warring parties agree to three-day truce.

text.p: The warring parties in the Congo Republic's capital Brazzaville agreed to a three-day truce on Tuesday and a demilitarisation of the international airport, a focus of fighting in the city, the French ambassador said.
Raymond Cesaire told Reuters across the river in Kinshasa by telephone that the truce would take effect at midnight and the two sides had agreed to recognise the airport as a neutral zone.

French troops are withdrawing from Brazzaville after evacuating more than 5,000 French and other foreign nationals trapped by almost two weeks of ethnic and political clashes between supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.

"A colonel from President Lissouba's force and from Sassou's force signed the agreement, so did a colonel from Kolelas's group," Cesaire said after a two-hour meeting at the French embassy organised by the National Mediation Committee.
Brazzaville mayor Bernard Kolelas, whose supporters were at the heart of 1993 clashes that killed at least 2,000 people, heads the committee. His militia has stayed clear of the fighting this time.

Cesaire said military observers from both sides would monitor the demilitarisation of the airport zone and a further meeting would be held on Wednesday to discuss the situation. "It will allow the airport to be used as a base for humanitarian operations," he added.
